chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Salih ibn Uqba from Bashir al-Dahhan who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I miss the Hajj, so I go to recognize [the grave] at the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' He said, 'Well done, O Bashir! Whoever of the believers comes to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), recognizing his right, on a day other than the day of Eid, Allah will write for him twenty Hajjs and twenty Umrahs, properly performed and accepted; and twenty Hajjs and Umrahs with a sent Prophet or a just Imam. And whoever comes to him on the day of Eid, Allah will write for him one hundred Hajjs and one hundred Umrahs and one hundred military expeditions with a sent Prophet or a just Imam.'

I said to him, 'How is it for me with the likes of the Standing (at Arafat)?' He looked at me as if slightly angry, then said to me, 'O Bashir! Indeed, when the believer comes to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of Arafah, and performs Ghusl from the Euphrates, then turns his face towards him, Allah will write for him, with every step, a Hajj with its rituals — and I do not know except that he said: 'And a military expedition.'

key_terms.الْمَوْقِفُ: The Standing (referring to the ritual standing at Arafat during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the theological elevation of Karbala as a spiritual axis, where the grave of Imam Al-Husayn (as) serves as a substitute for major acts of worship. The distinction between regular visits and the 'Day of Eid' (often interpreted as the anniversary of his martyrdom or a specific festive occasion) underscores the concept of *I'tiraf bi-hiqqihi* (acknowledging his right/status), linking physical pilgrimage to spiritual recognition. The specific mention of the Euphrates (*Al-Furat*) for Ghusl on the Day of Arafah connects the ritual purity of the Imam's resting place to the cosmic significance of the Prophet's pilgrimage, reinforcing the Shia view of the Ahl al-Bayt's central role in salvation history.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba,, from Bashir Al Dahhhan who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Sometimes I miss the Hajj, so I go over to the grave of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Well done, O Bashir! Whichever Believer goes to the grave of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, recognising his<sup>asws</sup> right during other than the day of Eid, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him twenty Hajjs, and twenty Umrahs, properly performed, Accepted; and twenty Hajj and Umra with a Mursil Prophet<sup>as</sup>, or a Just Imam<sup>asws</sup>. And the one who goes to him<sup>asws</sup> on the day of Eid, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him one hundred Hajj, and one hundred Umrah, and one hundred military expeditions with a Mursil Prophet<sup>as</sup>, or a just Imam<sup>asws</sup>’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How is it for me with the likes of the Pausing Station (like Arafaat)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> looked at me resembling the anger, then said to me: ‘O Bashir! The Believer, when he goes to the grave of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> on the day of Arafaat, and washes from the Euphrates, then diverts (his attention) to him<sup>asws</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him, with every step taken, a Hajj with its rituals’ – and I do not know except that he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And a military expedition’’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah from Bashir al-Dahhan who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I may miss performing al-Hajj, so I spend the day of ‘Arafah near the gravesite of al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam .’ He (the Imam) said, ‘That is very good, O Bashir. If anyone of believing people visits the gravesite of al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, with proper awareness of his rights on a day other than the day of ‘Id, Allah writes for him the reward for twenty Hajjah. (He writes for him) the reward for twenty accepted ‘Umrah, well-performed, twenty Hajjah and al-‘Umrah in the company of a prophet who is sent as a messenger and an Imam of justice. If one visits his gravesite on the day of Td, Allah writes for him the reward for one hundred Hajjah, one hundred ‘Umrah, one hundred times an armed campaign against the enemies of Allah in support of a prophet who is sent as a messenger or an Imam of justice.’

I (the narrator) then asked, ‘How can this be for me like staying in ‘Arafat?’ He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) looked at me as if with anger then said, ‘O Bashir, take notice of this. When a believing person comes to the gravesite of al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, on the day of ‘Arafah, after taking a bath in al-Furat and comes to him, Allah writes for him for every step, one Hajjah performed with its acts’ - I do not know else, except, until he said, ‘and an armed campaign against the enemies of Allah.’”
